description: We are a team of curious, creative, and driven young innovators of freshman high school passionate about space exploration, scientific discovery, and the stories behind humanity’s journey beyond Earth. Through “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” we aim to answer the question "What happens to a space mission after its equipment stops working — or its mission ends?". We are gonna help students explore real spacecraft and robotic explorers, discover what they achieved.
summary:
Project 926 is a project created by a group of high school freshmen, inspired by NASA’s space exploration missions. Our goal is to bring attention to space equipment, especially the Opportunity Mars Rover, and help students understand its importance.

Our project includes a rover model, an interactive website, a PowerPoint presentation, and a short demonstration video. The website allows students to explore the rover’s different parts, discover interesting facts, understand the tools it used, and learn about its achievements.

By combining technology, creativity, and hands-on learning, Project 926 aims to make space exploration more exciting and inspire a new generation of young scientists and space enthusiasts.

Project 926 wants to make space exploration more fun and encourage the group of young scientists and people who love space. Created by students, for a better future.
details:
What does it do? How does it work?

The project consists of an educational website and a physical rover model. The website allows students to explore the Opportunity Rover, learn about its scientific instruments, discover its mission history and understand its contributions to Mars exploration.

Interactive features such as a Heritage Dashboard, mission timeline, photo gallery and educational quiz make learning about space technology simple, interesting and enjoyable. The physical rover model provides students with a hands-on understanding of the rover's structure and components.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

The project makes complex scientific information easier for school students to understand. It encourages curiosity, creativity, and an interest in science, technology, engineering, and astronomy. Its main objective is to preserve the legacy of NASA missions while inspiring young learners to explore space and consider future careers in STEM fields.

Tools, technologies and resources used

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to develop the educational website. Canva and PowerPoint were used for presentations, while CapCut helped us edit videos. Our research was supported by NASA's official mission data, photographs, and Planetary Data System resources. The physical prototype was created using affordable, easily available materials such as cardboard, plastic bottle caps, paper, clay, and other craft supplies.

What makes our project creative?

Our creativity lies in combining digital learning with physical exploration. Instead of simply presenting facts about the Opportunity Rover, we allow students to interact with its features through an educational website while also examining a physical model. This combination transforms complex space technology into an engaging, interactive and memorable learning experience.

Factors considered by our team

Our team prioritized scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language, accessibility, affordability, creativity, and ease of use. We wanted to ensure that the project was understandable and engaging for school students while maintaining accuracy through reliable NASA data and resources.

Our Vision

As students, we aim to inspire the next generation to explore the wonders of space, embrace curiosity, and think beyond boundaries. Through this project, we hope to show that the achievements of past missions can spark new ideas, encourage innovation, and shape the future of space exploration.

Inspired by yesterday's discoveries, driven by tomorrow's possibilities.
